text:
alertbot: [INCIDENT] Elevated 5xx + timeouts observed for customer MarlinData on dedicated-usw2-marlin-01. Trigger: gateway proxies reporting increased 502/504 and backend timeouts. Paging on-call.

Sara (oncall): just got paged, I'm on it. any customer-facing impact reported? :eyes:

Liz (Support): MarlinData reported slow response on /v1/generate and ~20% errors when traffic peaks. They say it's intermittent since ~10:12 UTC.

Sara (oncall): ok grabbing metrics. Mike can you pull proxy/gateway 5xx rates and queue depth for that cluster?

Mike (SRE): looking now — gateway 5xx rate spiked at 10:11 -> 42% for marlin route, overall cluster CPU ~88%, GPU util for pool A ~97%. KV eviction rate is elevated on node group mgmt-ks-* with lots of page faults.

Jesse (Infra): seeing sustained disk IO and OOM kill hints in kubelet logs for pods pinned to node-03. suspect noisy tenant process hogging GPU memory/streams.

Sara (oncall): probable noisy neighbor (large long-running generative jobs) causing KV/kv-cache evictions and request queuing -> timeouts at gateway. Need immediate mitigation to restore customer service.

PD-Bot: incident acknowledged by Sara (oncall). Escalation level: P2. Handoff to on-call SRE team.

Mike (SRE): temporary mitigations we can try in parallel: 1) soft-rate-limit MarlinData to reduce pressure, 2) reroute Marlin traffic to a warm spare cluster (dedicated-usw2-spare-01) with fallback model, 3) evict suspected noisy pods. Which should we run first?

Sara (oncall): do safe steps first — soft-rate-limit at the gateway and enable fallback routing. evict only if needed. Liz, warn customer about transient throttle?

Liz (Support): messaging sent to MarlinData: "We've detected elevated errors on your Dedicated cluster and are applying temporary throttling and routing. No data loss expected. We'll update in 15 mins."

Mike (SRE): applying soft rate limit now for marlin tenant at edge layer: 
```bash
rctl tenant update marlin --rate-limit 120rps
```
Applying...

Mike (SRE): rate-limit applied at 10:23:15 UTC. Observing immediate drop in request queue depth, gateway 5xx down to ~28% now.

Jesse (Infra): initiating reroute to spare cluster for non-stream requests. Using routing policy 'fallback-evacuate-small' which maps large streaming sessions to standby. Command: 
```bash
rcli route set --tenant marlin --from dedicated-usw2-marlin-01 --to dedicated-usw2-spare-01 --filter 'content_type!=stream'
```
Executing and watching healthchecks.

Ben (Platform): FYI spare cluster has capacity for light/medium workloads but not heavy streaming. We'll serve reduced model (quantized v2-small) to avoid GPU saturation.

Mike (SRE): gateway 5xx now down to ~12% and falling. Errors are mostly 504/timeouts from backends that exceeded configured idle. Queue depth normalized.

Sara (oncall): good. keep routing and rate-limit for 10-15 mins, let metrics settle. If errors <5% for 5m we can keep rolling.

Liz (Support): MarlinData acknowledged and says latency improved for some requests, still seeing timeouts for long streaming sessions. They asked if we can prioritize big jobs.

Jesse (Infra): found a set of long-running jobs (k8s pods) from tenant "marlin-analytics" consuming multiple GPUs and not honoring preemption. Listing: 
```bash
kubectl get pods -n marlin | grep longjob
# marlin-analytics-longjob-7f8  Running  4/4  3h
```
We can evict those if customer agrees.

Sara (oncall): do not evict customer-owned pods without consent. Are these part of MarlinData production workload or user-initiated experiments?

Liz (Support): asking Marlin now if the long jobs are expected. ETA 5m.

PD-Bot: paging escalation: add Jesse to incident if evictions needed.

Mike (SRE): while we wait, I'm increasing KV cache max size for cluster to reduce thrashing: 
```bash
redwoodctl config set cluster dedicated-usw2-marlin-01 kv_cache.max_entries=120000 --apply
```
That should reduce backend cold-starts for a bit. Applied at 10:31:40 UTC.

Mike (SRE): metrics: 5xx down to 6% overall, tail latencies still high for streaming. CPU/GPU utilization easing.

Liz (Support): Marlin replied: the long jobs are their nightly analytics — they didn't expect them to run right now. They're okay with us pausing/evicting to restore production. Give us the exact command and we'll ack.

Sara (oncall): proceed with eviction but use graceful termination where possible. coordinate with Jesse.

Jesse (Infra): evicting long jobs now with graceful downscale: 
```bash
kubectl delete pod marlin-analytics-longjob-7f8 -n marlin --grace-period=30
```
Pod deletion started 10:35:02 UTC. Watching scheduler.

Mike (SRE): after eviction: GPU util dropped to 62%, KV evictions down 90%. Gateway 5xx trended to <1.5% within 5 minutes.

Sara (oncall): excellent. set incident status to mitigated, keep rate limit and routing in place for 30 more minutes, then we can gradually remove. create a short post-action note for customer.

Liz (Support): sent message: "We've evicted a long-running analytics job which restored performance to production endpoints. We'll coordinate a schedule for heavy analytics runs so they don't overlap peak traffic." Customer thanked us.

Ben (Platform): creating follow-up runbook item: detect noisy-tenant pattern (sustained GPU >90% + KV evictions + queue growth) -> automated soft-quota + notify tenant + optional eviction after consent window. Filing ticket INF-7823.

Mike (SRE): logs/ops snippets saved to incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/2991234567/raw-logs.tar.gz. Linking to postmortem.

Sara (oncall): handoff to next oncall in 30m. PD-Bot: add follow-up tasks and owner.

PD-Bot: Follow-up tasks created: INF-7823 (platform runbook), PM-4531 (customer scheduling), OWNER: Jesse.

Sara (oncall): final customer impact note for postmortem: MarlinData experienced elevated 5xx and timeouts for ~23 minutes during 10:11-10:34 UTC, primarily affecting streaming endpoints; bulk of user-facing traffic restored after rate-limiting + reroute + eviction. No data loss. Estimated 3% of total requests failed during window.

Liz (Support): passing to account team to review credits and scheduling.

Jesse (Infra): I'll draft a short remediation doc and add an auto-detect rule for noisy-job patterns.

Sara (oncall): thanks team. I'm closing this thread and will attach the mitigations to the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

alertbot: Incident P2 -> mitigated. Close time 10:48 UTC.
